notes: The manual describes cheaper pricing at higher volumes but supplies no numerical saturation point or procedure defining when further discounts stop.
Finding the most frequent shopper interaction uses only the schema and ordinary counting.
Merchant-month volume and fraud metrics select multi-criterion fee rules for individual payments before their fees are summed.
The maximum euro amount is available from a schema column without additional domain logic.
Each eligible NexPay credit fee uses the single fixed-plus-variable expression, after which selecting the largest fee and its ACI requires no additional domain computation.
March merchant aggregates must be computed and applied back to payments while matching all fee-rule criteria to identify applicable IDs.
The fixed-plus-variable fee is evaluated for GlobalCard credit rules and then averaged across those rules.
Full June volume and fraud metrics determine payment-level rule eligibility before matched transaction fees are summed.
The supplied merchant categories select compatible SwiftCharge rules, whose single-expression fees are averaged without computing merchant-month eligibility.
Monthly eligibility metrics support rematching fraudulent payments under alternative ACIs and comparing their aggregate fees.
The affected payments must be found through monthly rule eligibility before their rate-change fee differences are calculated and summed.
Identifying affected merchants requires applying rule 709 to payments using full-month aggregates and its other eligibility criteria.
April merchant aggregates determine eligibility while fraudulent transactions are repriced under candidate ACIs and their total fees compared.
Fees for the selected day still require full natural-month eligibility metrics before transaction-level rule matching and summation.
Merchant averages and their ranking require no knowledge beyond the payment amount and merchant columns.
Counting transactions by their IP country uses only schema information.
Monthly eligibility and payment-level matching identify uses of rule 64 before the changed variable-rate costs are summed.
Fees at the fixed transaction value are computed for rules and averaged by scheme before choosing the largest scheme average.
Monthly metrics support baseline and changed-MCC rule matching, two fee calculations and their aggregated difference.
The average transaction amount is a direct aggregation of the euro amount column.
Rule 787 must be matched to eligible payments using monthly metrics before their variable-rate fee differences are aggregated.
Compatible GlobalCard rules are selected for account type F, their fees are calculated and those rule-level fees are averaged.
Only direct membership filters on fee-rule category lists, including their explicitly defined wildcard values, are needed.
Rule fees can be calculated and compared by MCC, but the manual does not specify how fees across differing rule conditions should represent an MCC in general.
Distinct merchant names require only the merchant column.
The account and MCC categories select compatible GlobalCard rules, and their fixed-amount transaction fees are computed and averaged.
Full-month merchant metrics and payment attributes must jointly satisfy rule 1 before affected merchants can be identified.
July eligibility aggregates must be retained while fraudulent payments are rematched to alternative ACI rules and their total costs compared.
May merchant-level aggregates determine applicable multi-field rules before individual payment fees are computed and summed.
The tenth day's payments must be matched against fee rules using full January aggregates rather than aggregates for that day alone.
Checking equality across all transaction columns requires no domain-manual computation.
The needed knowledge selects compatible NexPay account-type rules and computes one fee per rule before averaging.
Applicable IDs for the selected day require full calendar-month metrics and multi-field matching of that day's payments to fee rules.
Rule-level fees at the fixed amount are averaged by card scheme before selecting the smallest scheme average.
The original and hypothetical MCC require separate rule matches and fee calculations using monthly metrics before computing the annual difference.
Finding rule IDs only requires category-list membership filters and the explicit empty-list wildcard convention.
The most commonly used card scheme follows from direct transaction counts by the schema category.
Monthly eligibility metrics support repricing payments with both the original and proposed MCC before their annual fee difference is calculated.
